headline: Weeks at No. 1 don't decide Entertainer of the Year. Weeks in the top 5 almost always do
dek: The act with the most top 5 weeks has won 14 of the last 16 Entertainer races. The act with the most weeks at No. 1 has won only seven.
body: Entertainer of the Year is the biggest award at the Willboard Country Awards, and the hardest to call from the chart. Is it about No. 1s, weeks on top, or just being everywhere? We went back through all 16 Entertainer races from 2010 to 2025 and compared every nominee's Hot 20 record in the 12 months before each show, from November through October. We looked at five measures: No. 1 hits, weeks at No. 1, weeks in the top 5, chart entries and total weeks on the chart. Where an act had more than one song charting, each song's weeks count separately.

The headline number. The nominee with the most top 5 weeks has won Entertainer 14 times in 16 years. Most No. 1 hits comes next, but only when you count ties: the winner had the most No. 1s, or shared the lead, 12 times. Weeks at No. 1, the stat that sounds the most important, is the weakest. The nominee who spent the most weeks on top has won only seven times.

Wins without the most weeks on top. [[Carrie Underwood]], the only three-time winner, shows the pattern best. In 2023 she won with just two weeks at No. 1, while [[Kip Moore]] had nine. What she did have was 26 top 5 weeks, the most in the field. [[Leann Rimes]] beat [[Craig Campbell]] in 2014 with 25 top 5 weeks to his 18, even though Campbell spent 12 weeks at No. 1 to her 10. In 2022, [[Carly Pearce]] led with 24 top 5 weeks and won, while [[Runaway June]] had the most weeks at No. 1 with seven. Last year [[Ella Langley]] won with only three weeks at No. 1, against Pearce's eight, because she had 35 top 5 weeks to Pearce's 29.

The two exceptions. In 2017, Little Big Town led the field with 18 top 5 weeks, but Miranda Lambert won with 16. She had the most weeks at No. 1 that year with 10, so she still led on another major measure. The real upset came in 2015. Rimes won with just five top 5 weeks, the fewest in the field, and one week at No. 1. Kacey Musgraves led with 17 top 5 weeks without a single No. 1, and Tyler Farr had nine weeks on top. Nothing on the chart points to Rimes that year.

This year's field. Here's how the 2026 nominees stack up from November 2025 through the Oct. 22 chart. Ella Langley has 38 top 5 weeks, four No. 1s and 13 weeks at No. 1. [[Megan Moroney]] has 28 top 5 weeks, two No. 1s and eight weeks on top. [[Kacey Musgraves]] has 25 top 5 weeks, two No. 1s and seven weeks on top. [[Zach Top]] has 21, two and seven. Carly Pearce has seven, one and two.

By the measure that has called 14 of the last 16 races, Langley leads the field. But the stat said the same about Musgraves in 2015, and Rimes won anyway. We'll find out on Nov. 18, the night the CMA Awards air.

linkText: See every song that debuted at No. 1
headline: Thirty-one songs have debuted at No. 1 on the Pop 10. A record six of them arrived in 2025
dek: Some opened at the top and stayed for months, and one lasted a single week. Here's the history of the Pop 10's instant No. 1s. Updated Oct. 30 with Kayla Rae's ‘It Wasn't Nothing.’
body: Since the Pop 10 launched on Oct. 27, 2011, 31 songs have entered the chart at No. 1. That leaves out the launch week itself, when every song on the chart was new. Drake and Rihanna's ‘Take Care’ was the first, on Feb. 9, 2012. The most recent is [[Kayla Rae]]'s ‘It Wasn't Nothing,’ which opened at No. 1 on Oct. 29, 2026, the week after this story first ran.

The longest stay. [[Bruno Mars]] set the bar early. ‘Locked Out of Heaven’ debuted at No. 1 on Oct. 18, 2012 and stayed there for its first 11 weeks. No other song that debuted on top has come close: the next-longest opening streaks are six weeks, by [[Macklemore]] and Ryan Lewis's ‘Can't Hold Us’ (2013), [[The Chainsmokers]] and Halsey's ‘Closer’ (2016), Julia Michaels's ‘Worst In Me’ (2017) and The Chainsmokers' ‘High’ (2022). ‘Locked Out of Heaven’ is also the third-longest-running No. 1 of any kind on the Pop 10, behind only ‘Somebody That I Used To Know’ (15 weeks) and ‘Habit’ (14).

Short visits. Opening at No. 1 doesn't guarantee a long run. [[Meghan Trainor]]'s ‘No Excuses’ debuted on top on March 8, 2018 and fell to No. 2 the next week; it's the only one of the first 30 that spent just one week at No. 1. Logic's ‘1-800-273-8255,’ with Alessia Cara and Khalid, held No. 1 for two weeks in 2017 but spent only three weeks on the chart in all, the shortest stay of the group.

Two that came back. Two songs lost the top spot right away and then returned. Cassandra Coleman's ‘Night Air’ debuted at No. 1 on May 4, 2023, slipped to No. 2, and went on to spend four weeks at No. 1 over a 16-week run. Shkodra Elektronike's ‘Zjerm,’ Albania's 2025 Eurovision entry, did the same: it debuted on top on May 15, 2025, dropped to No. 2, and finished with three weeks at No. 1.

Repeat offenders. Three acts have debuted at No. 1 twice. [[Zara Larsson]] did it with ‘Lush Life’ (2016) and ‘Ruin My Life’ (2018), and The Chainsmokers with ‘Closer’ (2016) and ‘High’ (2022). [[Ariana Grande]] did it in back-to-back years: ‘We Can't Be Friends’ opened on top on March 14, 2024 and held No. 1 for five straight weeks, and ‘Twilight Zone’ followed on April 3, 2025 with four.

2025, the year of the instant No. 1. No year has more than 2025's six. Besides ‘Twilight Zone’ and ‘Zjerm,’ there were Chappell Roan's ‘The Subway’ in August, [[Demi Lovato]]'s ‘Let You Go’ in October, Chloe Tang and Casandra's ‘Running on Blue’ in December, and Peach PRC's ‘Out Loud’ on Christmas Day. The previous high was four, in 2017. The opposite is true too: 2015, 2019 and 2020 had none at all.

So far 2026 has four: [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis’ in March, Kim Petras's ‘Need for Speed’ in April, Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me,’ Romania's Eurovision entry, in May, and now Kayla Rae's ‘It Wasn't Nothing,’ her fourth No. 1 and the first time she has debuted on top. Whether any more arrive this year is up to Will's listening.

headline: Maddie & Tae are the most successful duo in Hot 20 history. Now Maddie Font is starting over on her own
dek: Her first solo EP, ‘Drive Me Around,’ arrives Nov. 6, and its title track is already on the chart. Here's the record she's stepping away from.
body: Last December, [[Maddie & Tae]] told People they would stop working as a duo after 15 years. Taylor Kerr is stepping back to focus on her family, and Maddie Font is carrying on alone, though both said they're leaving the door open to make music together again someday. Font's first solo single, ‘Drive Me Around,’ came out in September, and her debut EP of the same name follows on Nov. 6. It has four songs and is coming out independently.

The duo's numbers. Maddie & Tae put 24 songs on the Hot 20, and 12 of them reached No. 1. That's more than any other duo or group: [[Lady A]] is next with 10. Only [[Carrie Underwood]] (21) and [[Carly Pearce]] (18) have more No. 1s, and [[Kenny Chesney]] ties them at 12. Their songs spent 42 weeks at No. 1 and 413 weeks on the chart in all. The longest stay on top belongs to ‘Die From a Broken Heart,’ with seven weeks in 2018 and 2019.

A slow start, then a streak. Their first four singles all came close without reaching the top. ‘Girl In A Country Song’ peaked at No. 3 in 2014, then ‘Fly,’ ‘Shut Up and Fish’ and ‘Sierra’ all stopped at No. 2. ‘After the Storm Blows Through’ finally reached No. 1 in March 2017 and held it for four weeks. From October 2018 to November 2020, they were on the chart for 108 straight weeks, and that run produced five No. 1s, from ‘Die From a Broken Heart’ to ‘Water in His Wine Glass.’

The awards shelf. At the Willboard Country Awards, Maddie & Tae won Vocal Duo/Group of the Year seven times: in 2016, then every year from 2019 through 2024. They also won Entertainer of the Year twice, in 2019 and 2020. They're nominated for Vocal Duo/Group again this year, and the winners will be revealed Nov. 18, the night the CMA Awards air.

The last duo hit. Their final Hot 20 appearance was as guests on [[Colbie Caillat]]'s ‘Live Without,’ which reached No. 3 and left the chart after Feb. 5. That was the last time either of them was on the Hot 20 until this month, an eight-month gap.

Font on her own. ‘Drive Me Around,’ which she wrote with Jonathan Singleton and Brent Anderson, entered at No. 19 on Oct. 8, held there the next week, and moved to No. 18 on Oct. 22. The EP also has ‘Make It Up To Me,’ ‘All The Red In California’ and ‘When A Woman Stops Crying.’ That last song is a co-write with Anna Vaus and Taylor Kerr, so the duo's story isn't over on paper either.
Font is starting her solo career with a record that only two acts in Hot 20 history have topped. How the new songs do on the chart is up to Will's listening.

linkText: See the longest runs on the chart
headline: Carly Pearce owns two of the three longest runs in Hot 20 history. The secret is timing, not volume
dek: She stayed on the chart for 116 straight weeks, then 122, almost always with just one song at a time. Here's how the handoffs worked.
body: Only one act has stayed on the Hot 20 longer without a break than [[Carly Pearce]]: [[Ella Langley]], whose run reached 131 straight weeks this month and is still going. Behind her, Pearce holds second and third place, with 122 weeks from March 14, 2024 to July 16, 2026, and 116 weeks from February 25, 2021 to May 11, 2023. [[Kenny Chesney]] (109), [[Maddie & Tae]] (108) and [[Carrie Underwood]] (104) are the only other acts to pass 100. Nobody else has done it twice.

One song at a time. You might expect a streak like that to come from flooding the chart. It didn't. In the 116-week run, Pearce had exactly one song on the Hot 20 in 99 of those weeks, and she never had three at once. The 122-week run was the same story: one song in 81 weeks, never more than two. What kept her there was the timing of each new single.

The first run: five No. 1s and a No. 2. ‘Messy’ started it in February 2021 and reached No. 1. It left the chart on July 1, and ‘29’ arrived the very next week. ‘Never Wanted To Be That Girl,’ her duet with [[Ashley McBryde]], overlapped ‘29’ that fall, and on January 27, 2022, it left the same week ‘Diamondback’ came in. ‘What He Didn't Do’ and ‘All the Whiskey In the World’ each overlapped the song before them by a few weeks. Five of the six songs went to No. 1, and ‘All the Whiskey’ peaked at No. 2. When it fell off after May 11, 2023, nothing was waiting behind it, and Pearce spent 43 weeks off the chart.

The second run: six straight No. 1s. ‘Hummingbird’ ended the break on March 14, 2024 and became the first of six No. 1s in a row: ‘Hummingbird,’ ‘My Place,’ ‘Truck on Fire,’ ‘Oklahoma,’ ‘If Looks Could Kill’ and ‘No Rain.’ Some handoffs had room to spare, with ‘Truck on Fire’ and ‘Oklahoma’ sharing the chart for nine weeks. Others were as tight as they come. ‘If Looks Could Kill’ left on August 28, 2025 and ‘No Rain’ debuted a week later. ‘No Rain’ left on January 1, 2026 and ‘Dream Come True’ debuted on January 8. Her guest spot on [[Jordan Davis]]'s ‘Mess with Missing You’ added a second song that fall.

How it ended. The run held on through two top-10 singles, ‘Dream Come True’ and ‘If I Don't Leave I'm Gonna Stay’ with [[Riley Green]], each peaking at No. 10. When ‘If I Don't Leave’ fell off after July 16, 2026, Pearce missed exactly one chart. ‘She Don't’ debuted on July 30, so a single week stands between her and an unbroken run of more than two and a half years. ‘She Don't’ is No. 9 this week, in its 12th week, and that's a new run of 12 and counting.

The bigger picture. Since her first Hot 20 week on June 29, 2017, Pearce has been on the chart for 424 of its 872 weeks, almost exactly half of them. She has 24 entries and 18 No. 1s. Long runs on the Hot 20 don't come from stacking songs. They come from having the next one ready the week the last one leaves.

headline: Two No. 1 acts have new albums out this month. One hasn't charted since 2019; the other just had a No. 1
dek: Brothers Osborne released ‘Watertown’ on Oct. 23, and Kaitlin Butts follows with ‘Hello, Honky Tonk’ on Oct. 30. Here's what each one has done on the Hot 20.
body: October ends with back-to-back Fridays of new country music from two acts who have both topped the Hot 20. [[Brothers Osborne]] released their fifth studio album, ‘Watertown,’ on MCA on Oct. 23. Jay Joyce produced the 11 songs, and the title nods to the Osborne brothers' roots in the blue-collar waterfront town of Deale, Maryland. A week later, on Oct. 30, [[Kaitlin Butts]] releases ‘Hello, Honky Tonk’ on Republic Records, previewed by ‘I Wanna Be Bad.’ Their recent Hot 20 runs couldn't be more different.

Brothers Osborne: a slow climb to the top. The duo arrived in June 2015 with ‘Stay A Little Longer,’ which entered at No. 20 and took 18 weeks to reach No. 1, on Oct. 22, 2015. It spent one week on top, 20 weeks on the chart in all, and finished No. 26 for the year. Their next two singles both peaked at No. 4: ‘21 Summer’ in 2016 and ‘It Ain't My Fault’ in 2017. Two of their seven Hot 20 entries are guest spots, on David Nail's ‘Good At Tonight’ (No. 8) and Dierks Bentley's ‘Burning Man’ (No. 7).

Then they went quiet. Their last Hot 20 entry, ‘I Don't Remember Me (Before You),’ peaked at No. 7 and fell off in May 2019. That's more than seven years without them on the chart. Their debut album, ‘Pawn Shop,’ which carried three of their Hot 20 hits, is still their most-played album on Willboard, with 1,457 plays.

Kaitlin Butts: one of the slowest climbs ever. ‘Marfa Lights’ entered at No. 20 in January 2022 and needed 26 weeks to reach No. 1, on July 7, 2022. Only five of the Hot 20's 336 No. 1s took longer, and ‘Drunk Girl’ is the only other one that also took 26. ‘Marfa Lights’ stayed on the chart for 30 weeks and finished 2022 at No. 7 on the Year-End list. Her follow-up, ‘She's Using,’ reached No. 9 that fall.

And a No. 1 this year. Butts never really left. She's the featured voice on [[Flatland Cavalry]]'s ‘A Life Where We Work Out,’ which entered at No. 17 on April 2 and reached No. 1 on July 30, its 18th week. It returned to the top on Aug. 27 for a second week at No. 1, and it spent 28 weeks on the chart before falling off this month. That gives her two Hot 20 No. 1s, four years apart, and puts ‘Hello, Honky Tonk’ out while her latest hit is still fresh.

Familiar names in the credits. ‘Watertown’ has two guests with Willboard history. Cody Johnson sings on the opener, ‘Born and Raised Hell’; his only Hot 20 entry, ‘With You I Am,’ reached No. 7 in 2017. Stephen Wilson Jr. appears on ‘Tough Kid,’ and he's the more recent chart-topper: his duet with Lori McKenna, ‘The Tunnel,’ spent six weeks at No. 1 from December 2024 into January 2025.
Both of these acts took the long road to No. 1 the first time. Which songs from these albums reach the chart, if any, is up to Will's listening.

headline: Ten years ago this week: Tim McGraw ran the Hot 20, and a future seven-week No. 1 entered at No. 17
dek: A look back at the Hot 20 and Pop 10 of Oct. 27, 2016, and where those songs and artists went next.
body: Ten years ago this week, the Hot 20 of Oct. 27, 2016 belonged to [[Tim McGraw]]. ‘How I'll Always Be’ held No. 1 for the second of its three weeks on top. McGraw was also all over the rest of the chart. He was featured on Big & Rich's ‘Lovin' Lately’ at No. 4 and on Florida Georgia Line's ‘May We All’ at No. 20, so he had three songs in the Hot 20 at once.

The debut that mattered. The quietest move on the chart turned out to be the biggest. [[Little Big Town]]'s ‘Better Man’ entered at No. 17. Nine weeks later, on Dec. 29, it reached No. 1, and it stayed there for seven weeks, through Feb. 16, 2017. It finished as the No. 6 song of 2017 and won Music Video of the Year at the 2017 Willboard Country Awards, where it was also up for Song and Single of the Year.

The rest of the top 5. [[Miranda Lambert]]'s ‘Vice’ sat at No. 2 and reached No. 1 two weeks later, on Nov. 10, for two weeks. Lambert is still charting a decade later. Her 34th entry, ‘Two Things Can Be True,’ debuted on this week's Hot 20. [[Chris Stapleton]]'s ‘Parachute’ was at No. 3 after a week at No. 1, and Jennifer Nettles's ‘Stupid Girl’ was at No. 5 after two weeks on top.

Who was just getting started. [[Maren Morris]] was in her first year on the chart, with ‘80s Mercedes’ at No. 7. It peaked at No. 3. [[Jon Pardi]] was at No. 19 with ‘Dirt On My Boots,’ which peaked at No. 17. He's charted 15 times since 2013, most recently with ‘She Drives Away’ this January. [[Dolly Parton]]'s ‘Pure and Simple’ was at No. 13 on its way to a No. 4 peak.
Who wasn't. Florida Georgia Line's ‘May We All’ was the duo's seventh and final Hot 20 entry. It peaked at No. 11, and they never reached No. 1.

Over on the Pop 10. [[Meghan Trainor]] and Yo Gotti's ‘Better’ took over at No. 1 that week and held it for two weeks. It knocked off [[The Weeknd]]'s ‘Starboy,’ down to No. 3 after two weeks on top. Just below, ‘Starving’ by Hailee Steinfeld, Grey and Zedd sat at No. 5 after four weeks at No. 1. It finished as the No. 6 pop song of 2016. Maroon 5 and Kendrick Lamar's ‘Don't Wanna Know’ was at No. 2, and Alessia Cara's ‘Scars to Your Beautiful’ was at No. 8 in its second week.
A different era. In 2016, the Pop 10 was still built by feel. Play tracking didn't arrive until December 2017. The Hot 20 has ranked songs by plays since its first week in 2010.

headline: The CMA Awards and the Hot 20 agree on Ella Langley. They don't agree on much else
dek: With CMA voting closing Oct. 27, we checked every nominee for country's biggest night against a year of Willboard charts.
body: The 60th CMA Awards are set for Nov. 18 in Nashville, with Lainey Wilson hosting. Final-round voting closes on Oct. 27. Ella Langley leads the nominations with nine, followed by Miranda Lambert with seven and Kacey Musgraves with five. The CMAs are voted on by industry members and the Hot 20 is built from Will's own listening, so they were never going to line up exactly. Still, comparing the two says a lot about who's had the year on the radio and who's had it on the Hot 20.

Where they agree: Ella Langley. No act has owned the Hot 20 the way [[Ella Langley]] has. Since July 2025 she has logged 72 chart weeks across six songs, more than anyone else. Four of those songs reached No. 1, for 13 weeks on top between them: ‘Hungover,’ ‘Choosin' Texas’ (six weeks), ‘Be Her’ (three) and ‘Bottom of Your Boots,’ which is No. 1 again this week. Both of her Single of the Year nominees, ‘Be Her’ and ‘Choosin' Texas,’ were Hot 20 No. 1s. Nine nominations sounds like a lot until you look at that run.

The singles race. Only Langley's two Single of the Year nominees reached No. 1 on the Hot 20. Lainey Wilson's ‘Somewhere Over Laredo’ peaked at No. 5 and spent 29 weeks on the chart. Taylor Swift's ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ peaked at No. 6. Cody Johnson's ‘The Fall’ never charted. Musgraves's ‘Dry Spell’ is up for Song and Music Video of the Year after three weeks at No. 1 this spring, and Carly Pearce and Riley Green's ‘If I Don't Leave I'm Gonna Stay,’ a Musical Event nominee, reached No. 10.

The women's category is the closest match. Every Female Vocalist nominee has charted recently, and three of the five have had No. 1s in the past year: Langley and two more. [[Megan Moroney]] has two: ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress,’ whose seven weeks at No. 1 are the longest run on top this year. [[Kacey Musgraves]] has two as well, ‘Dry Spell’ and ‘Loneliest Girl,’ which held No. 1 for four weeks. [[Miranda Lambert]] just added her 34th career entry, ‘Two Things Can Be True.’ Lainey Wilson rounds out the field.

Where they don't agree: the men. The male side of the ballot looks very different from the Hot 20. Luke Combs, Chris Stapleton and Cody Johnson are all up for Entertainer of the Year, and none of them has had a Hot 20 entry since 2023. Stapleton's last was ‘White Horse,’ the same song that's up for Music Video of the Year. Johnson's only entry was ‘With You I Am’ in 2017. [[Zach Top]] is the exception. He's up for Male Vocalist and Album of the Year, and he's had two No. 1s since September 2025, ‘South of Sanity’ and ‘When You See Me.’ [[Stephen Wilson Jr]], up for Male Vocalist, New Artist, Song and Music Video, has one Hot 20 entry, and it was a big one: his duet with Lori McKenna, ‘The Tunnel,’ spent six weeks at No. 1 from December 2024 into January 2025.

New Artist. Two of the five New Artist nominees are on this week's chart. Emily Ann Roberts's ‘Laundry’ is at No. 4, her first entry, and Carter Faith's ‘If I Had Never Lost My Mind’ is at No. 19. Avery Anna and Tucker Wetmore haven't charted.

Who the CMAs left off. Some of the Hot 20's biggest acts this year aren't on the CMA ballot at all. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] has spent 56 weeks on the chart since July 2025, behind only Langley and Moroney and level with Musgraves. That includes the No. 1 ‘Jesus, I'm Jealous’ and the No. 2 ‘All In Already.’ [[Danielle Bradbery]]'s ‘Dent’ held No. 1 for five weeks this winter, and [[Ashley Cooke]]'s ‘Swear Words’ spent three weeks on top. [[The Castellows]] have logged 44 chart weeks without a CMA nomination for Vocal Group.

What it means. The CMAs and the Hot 20 measure different things. One reflects the industry's vote and the other reflects what Will kept coming back to. Where they overlap, though, it's hard to argue: Langley, Moroney and Musgraves have been everywhere on both. The Willboard Country Awards will have their own say. Until then, the CMAs air Nov. 18.

headline: Record of the Year almost always goes to the year's biggest hit. 2026 doesn't have one
dek: Fourteen shows of history, the stat that predicts the winner, and the front-runners, safe bets and dark horses for the 2027 Pop Awards.
body: Song of the Year asks what is on the page. Record of the Year asks about the finished record: how it sounds, how it was built and how hard it landed on the Pop 10. Like the Grammys, the Pop Awards honor the year before the show, so the 2027 show covers songs from roughly mid-November 2025 to mid-November 2026. Nominations aren't final, so this is a read of the field from the chart and from the records themselves. No song can be nominated twice, which rules out the 2026 show's nominees, among them ‘Bite My Tongue’ and ‘Let You Go.’ Agnes's ‘Ego’ sits right on the line, since its week at No. 1 came on Nov. 13, 2025.

The biggest hit usually wins. In 14 shows, the song that finished its eligibility year at No. 1 on the Year-End Pop 10 has won Record of the Year 12 times, from ‘Somebody That I Used to Know’ at the 2013 show to ‘Honesty’ at the 2026 show. The two upsets barely count as upsets. At the 2023 show, The Chainsmokers' ‘High’ beat 2022's No. 1, ‘Unholy,’ and at the 2025 show, Ariana Grande's ‘We Can't Be Friends’ beat 2024's No. 1, ‘Espresso.’ Both winners were the No. 2 song of their year. No record ranked lower than that has ever won.

What a winning run looks like. Record of the Year winners have averaged 7.4 weeks at No. 1, 14 weeks in the top 3 and 21 weeks on the chart. The nominees they beat averaged 3.4, 8 and 13. Weeks at No. 1 is a weaker predictor than you'd think, though: the winner led or tied its field there only 8 times in 14. Weeks in the top 3 is the stat that matters. The winner led or tied its field there 11 times. The clearest case is the 2018 show, where Demi Lovato's ‘Sorry Not Sorry’ won with a single week at No. 1 but 11 weeks in the top 3. Voters reward the record that was always there, not the one that peaked hardest.

2026 has no runaway hit. Four songs share the year's longest reign at four weeks each, and no contender is anywhere near the winners' average of 14 weeks in the top 3. The leaders are ‘Obsexxed’ and ‘Brutalist’ with nine each, then ‘Love4Life’ with eight. The lowest total any winner has had is nine, ‘High’ at the 2023 show. That makes this an unusually open race. It also means the Year-End list, which rewards staying power, will matter more than usual.

The December debut. Two of the last three winners had the same quiet advantage. Cassandra Coleman's ‘Habit’ debuted on Dec. 1, 2022, and Nelly Furtado's ‘Honesty’ debuted at No. 1 on Dec. 19, 2024. Both arrived just after a show's cutoff, so their entire runs counted toward the next year. Three songs have that advantage this time: Kayla Rae's ‘True’ (debuted at No. 2 on Dec. 4), ‘Running on Blue’ by [[Chloe Tang]] and Casandra (debuted at No. 1 on Dec. 11) and [[Peach PRC]]'s ‘Out Loud,’ which debuted at No. 1 on Christmas Day and held for three weeks. None of them had the staying power ‘Honesty’ did, though. ‘Honesty’ spent 24 weeks on the chart, and these ran 10, 6 and 8.

Dark horses get nominated. They don't win. ‘Catch My Breath’ made the 2014 field from No. 15 on the 2013 Year-End list, ‘Love Me Harder’ the 2016 field from No. 16, ‘Someone You Loved’ the 2020 field from No. 13, and ‘Ur So F**king Cool’ the 2021 field from No. 14. ‘Homura’ made the 2022 field without placing on the 2021 list at all. None of them came close to winning.

The front-runners. [[Chloe Tang]]'s ‘Obsexxed’ spent four weeks at No. 1 and nine in the top 3 across a 15-week run, the best all-round line in the field. Tang has built her sound on emotionally charged pop with a darker R&B edge, and this May single is where it finally clicked. ‘Running on Blue’ gave her a second No. 1 this year, which makes her one of only three acts with two, along with Petras and Coleman. [[Willa Ford]]'s ‘Love4Life’ held the top 3 for eight weeks. It's the comeback record of the year: Ford co-produced it with Gustav Afsahi and Jonathan Bluth for her album amanda, and one review singled out the shimmering '80s synth textures around its warm, grateful message. If history holds, the winner is one of these two.

The safe bets for a nomination. [[Kim Petras]]'s ‘Brutalist’ matches ‘Obsexxed’ with nine weeks in the top 3, built on a catchy beat that fades into a quiet, yearning ending. On the stat that matters most, it's a front-runner in all but name. [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis’ debuted at No. 1 and stayed four weeks; Matthew Koma and Brian Phillips produced it as the opener of an album Rolling Stone called a shimmering synth-pop comeback. Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me’ also debuted at No. 1 for four weeks. It's a nu-metal Eurovision entry, built from a beat producer Călin Grajdan had on his laptop, that finished third in Vienna. It's the boldest production in the field, though its title drew criticism that could give voters pause. [[Katy Perry]]'s ‘Bandaids’ has the longest run in the window at 16 weeks, a pop-rock ballad on which Perry traded synths for guitars and which Clash called a top-tier heartbreak anthem. And ‘Stateside + Zara Larsson’ is the best-built record of the year: [[Pink Pantheress]] and Oscar Scheller reworked the beat around Larsson's verse, stitching in Adina Howard's ‘Freak Like Me’ and Groove Armada's ‘I See You Baby.’

The dark horses. [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘End of Your Love’ is the one to watch, because its window is still open. It has spent the last three weeks at No. 1, and every week it adds before the cutoff counts. She co-produced it with Alec Shaw and recorded it with a full band in one room at Sound Emporium in Nashville. With ‘Habit’ at the 2024 show, she's also one of only three acts to win Record and Song of the Year on the same night, alongside Gotye and Maroon 5. Petras's ‘Need for Speed,’ made with Margo XS, Frost Children and nightfeelings, debuted at No. 1 and held three weeks but lasted only four on the chart, and it may split her support with ‘Brutalist.’ girlsweetvoiced's whispered ‘Cranberry’ had three weeks on top and seven in the top 3, proof that a quiet record can win the chart.

The verdict. On production alone, ‘Stateside’ and ‘Choke Me’ are the most striking records in the race. But Record of the Year has never been decided on sound alone, and in a year without a runaway hit, the top-3 count is the best guide. That points to ‘Obsexxed,’ with ‘Brutalist’ and ‘Love4Life’ close enough to make it a real contest. If there's a third upset in the show's history, look for it near the top of the Year-End list, not from a dark horse.

headline: Megan Moroney is nine for nine in the Hot 20's top 10
dek: ‘Medicine’ reaches No. 10, and every song she has charted has now made the top 10.
body: [[Megan Moroney]]'s ‘Medicine’ climbs 11-10 on this week's Hot 20. With that, all nine songs she has charted have reached the top 10. It's a perfect record that only a handful of acts have kept going this long.

The run so far. It started at the top. Her first entry, ‘Tennessee Orange,’ debuted in January 2023 and went all the way to No. 1, and ‘Traitor Joe’ followed it there that summer. ‘I'm Not Pretty’ peaked at No. 5 and ‘No Caller ID’ at No. 8. Then came four straight No. 1s: ‘Mama I Lied,’ ‘Am I Okay,’ ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress.’ That last one spent seven weeks on top this year, the longest stay at No. 1 of her career.

Six No. 1s from nine songs. Two thirds of everything she has released to the chart has gone to No. 1. ‘Medicine’ is the third charting song from her album Cloud 9, after ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress.’

The perfect-record club. Moroney joins a short list of acts with at least nine entries that all made the top 10. [[Kip Moore]] leads it by a wide margin: all 21 of his songs have reached the top 10, including ‘Faith in the Wind’ at No. 8 this week. [[George Strait]], [[Leann Rimes]] and [[Lainey Wilson]] are each 13 for 13, [[Chris Young]] is 11 for 11, and [[The Band Perry]] and [[Morgan Wade]] are 10 for 10.

Awards season. The timing doesn't hurt. Moroney goes into this year's Country Awards with five nominations, including her first for Entertainer of the Year, and ‘Wedding Dress’ is up for both Single and Song of the Year.

headline: Who will win at the 2026 Country Awards? Three experts make their picks
dek: A chart editor, a critic and a fan podcaster call the winners. They don't always agree.
body: The 2026 Country Awards nominations are set, so we asked three very different voices to call the winners. Mitzi Tallyho, Willboard's chart data editor, goes strictly by the past year on the Hot 20: No. 1s, weeks on top and staying power. Sebastian Crescendo, our senior music critic, cares about craft, meaning the writing, the singing and whether the record says something. Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, host of the fan podcast Windows Down, picks with the heart: the songs that got played the most in the car this year.

Entertainer of the Year. Tallyho picks [[Ella Langley]], and it isn't close on paper. She has four No. 1s and 13 weeks at No. 1 over the past year, the most of any nominee, and she's the reigning winner. Crescendo goes with [[Megan Moroney]]: “Cloud 9 is the sound of a writer who knows exactly who she is, and this is her first Entertainer nomination. Reward the leap.” Rhinestone picks [[Zach Top]]: “Two No. 1s, the most fun shows in country and a sound that makes 1995 feel brand new.”

Female Vocalist. Tallyho and Rhinestone both pick Langley. Crescendo stays with Moroney, pointing to the restraint of ‘Wedding Dress,’ which a quieter singer would have overplayed. Two votes to one for Langley.

Male Vocalist. Tallyho picks Zach Top, whose ‘South of Sanity’ and ‘When You See Me’ spent seven weeks at No. 1 between them. Crescendo picks [[David Nail]], whose cover of Bruce Cockburn's ‘Pacing the Cage’ reached No. 2: “It's the best vocal performance on the ballot, full stop.” Rhinestone picks [[Kip Moore]]: “Twenty-one songs, twenty-one top 10s. He's earned it.”

Vocal Duo/Group. Tallyho picks [[Flatland Cavalry]], the only nominee with a No. 1 this year (‘A Life Where We Work Out’ with Kaitlin Butts). Crescendo picks [[Maddie & Tae]]: “Their harmonies are still the gold standard, and they're the most decorated act in the show's history for a reason.” Rhinestone picks [[The Castellows]], whose ‘Love Is A Game’ is climbing the chart right now.

New Artist. Tallyho picks [[Mackenzie Carpenter]], who has a No. 1 (‘Jesus, I'm Jealous’) and two more top 5 hits this year. Crescendo likes Flatland Cavalry's songwriting depth. Rhinestone picks [[Kevin Powers]], whose ‘Move On’ with Shaboozey made it to No. 1.

Album of the Year. Tallyho picks Langley's Dandelion, which has sent three songs to No. 1 for a combined 12 weeks. Crescendo picks Moroney's Cloud 9, which reviewers called her most confident work. Rhinestone picks Top's Ain't In It For My Health.

Single of the Year. Tallyho picks ‘Wedding Dress,’ whose seven weeks at No. 1 are the most of any song on the ballot. Crescendo and Rhinestone both pick ‘Choosin' Texas,’ which Rhinestone calls “the song you sing along to with the windows down,” and Crescendo calls a classic country record in every sense.

Song of the Year. Here Tallyho and Crescendo agree: ‘Wedding Dress.’ For Crescendo, it's the writing of the year: a spare, acoustic song about realizing at the altar that you never got over the one who got away. It turns the fairy tale into something unsettling without a wasted line. Rhinestone goes with ‘Choosin' Texas,’ the story of losing a homesick partner to his Texas hometown and the woman waiting there, told from the long drive back east.

The consensus. Two of our three panelists land on Ella Langley for Female Vocalist and on ‘Wedding Dress’ for Song of the Year. Everything else is up for grabs, which is exactly how an awards night should feel.

headline: Miranda Lambert was there on day one. Her 34th Hot 20 entry proves she never left
dek: ‘Two Things Can Be True’ debuts at No. 20, putting her one entry behind Carrie Underwood's record.
body: [[Miranda Lambert]]'s ‘Two Things Can Be True’ enters the Hot 20 at No. 20 this week. It's her 34th entry, second only to [[Carrie Underwood]]'s 35. It extends a chart career that began the very first week the Hot 20 existed.

The first chart. When the Hot 20 began on January 28, 2010, Lambert had three songs on it: ‘White Liar’ at No. 3, plus ‘Dead Flowers’ and ‘Gunpowder & Lead.’ A few weeks later ‘The House That Built Me’ jumped from No. 18 to No. 2 in a single week. More than 16 years on, that's still the biggest one-week climb in the chart's history. It reached No. 1 three weeks after that.

The records. Lambert has 11 No. 1s and 28 total weeks at No. 1. ‘Over You’ ruled for nine weeks in 2012, the longest reign the Hot 20 has seen, a record it now shares with Kenny Chesney and Grace Potter's ‘You and Tequila’ and Kip Moore and Morgan Wade's ‘If I Was Your Lover.’ ‘Tin Man’ added eight more weeks in 2017. Her No. 1s span 15 years, from ‘The House That Built Me’ in 2010 to ‘Run’ in 2025.

Good company. She's also one of the chart's great collaborators. ‘We Were Us’ with Keith Urban and ‘Santa Fe’ with Parker McCollum both reached No. 2, and ‘Somethin' Bad’ with Carrie Underwood made No. 5. She even crossed over to the Pop 10, where ‘Drunk’ with Elle King peaked at No. 2 in 2021.

The count. At 34 entries, Lambert trails only Underwood. Her 11 No. 1s tie her with Kip Moore for fifth all-time, behind Underwood (21), Carly Pearce (18), Kenny Chesney (12) and Maddie & Tae (12). Sixteen years after she showed up on the very first chart, her story is still being written.

linkText: See all the 2026 Country Awards nominees
headline: Ella Langley leads the 2026 Country Awards nominations with six
dek: Megan Moroney, Kacey Musgraves and Zach Top follow with five each.
body: Last year's Entertainer of the Year, [[Ella Langley]], leads the 2026 Country Awards with six nominations: Entertainer, Female Vocalist, Album for Dandelion, Single and Song for “Choosin' Texas”, and Music Video for “Be Her”. She won four awards in 2025, including Entertainer and Female Vocalist.

[[Megan Moroney]], [[Kacey Musgraves]] and [[Zach Top]] have five nominations each, and all three join Langley in both Entertainer and Album. Moroney's “Wedding Dress”, which spent seven weeks at No. 1, is up for Single and Song, and this is her first Entertainer nomination. Musgraves is back in Entertainer for the first time since 2016, with “Loneliest Girl” up for Song. Top won Male Vocalist and New Artist last year and returns in Male Vocalist.

Several acts earn their first nominations. [[Kevin Powers]] leads them with four: Male Vocalist, New Artist, and Single and Musical Event for “Move On” with [[Shaboozey]]. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] has three (Female Vocalist, New Artist and Album for Hey Country Queen), as does [[Flatland Cavalry]] (Duo/Group, New Artist and Musical Event for “A Life Where We Work Out” with Kaitlin Butts). [[Danielle Bradbery]] picks up two, for Female Vocalist and “Dent” in Single.

The veterans are here too. [[Carly Pearce]], already the most nominated act in the show's history, adds two more for 40 in all, including her eighth Entertainer nomination. [[Maddie & Tae]], the show's biggest winners with 16 awards, return in Duo/Group.

headline: Song of the Year rarely goes to the biggest hit. Here's where the best writing of 2026 lives
dek: Fourteen shows say the chart barely matters in this category. A critic's read on the contenders for the 2027 Pop Awards.
body: Record of the Year rewards how a song sounds and how it landed. Song of the Year asks a harder question: what is actually on the page? The 2027 show covers songs from roughly mid-November 2025 to mid-November 2026, and nominations aren't final, so this is a look at the year's Pop 10 through that lens. No song can be nominated twice, so the 2026 show's nominees, among them ‘Bite My Tongue’ and ‘Let You Go,’ are out.

The chart barely matters here. Only three Song of the Year winners finished their year at No. 1 on the Year-End Pop 10: ‘Somebody That I Used to Know,’ ‘Love Somebody’ and ‘Habit.’ Those are also the only three times Song and Record of the Year have gone to the same song. Since the 2015 show, the two awards have split every year except 2024. The winners have come from all over the Year-End list, as high as No. 1 and as low as No. 32, and twice from off the list entirely. Two never reached No. 1 at all: The Chainsmokers' ‘Everybody Hates Me’ and Kayla Rae's ‘Get Close’ both peaked at No. 2.

What winners look like. Song of the Year winners have averaged 4.7 weeks at No. 1 and 8 weeks in the top 3. The nominees they beat averaged 3.0 and 7.0, which is almost the same. The winner led or tied its field in top-3 weeks only three times in 14 shows, and in weeks on the chart only twice. Compare Record of the Year, where the top-3 leader wins most years. The last two winners show the pattern. Cher's ‘DJ Play a Christmas Song’ won at the 2025 show on a three-week holiday run at No. 1, and Daughtry's ‘Antidote’ won at the 2026 show from No. 13 after just seven weeks on the chart. A long run gets a song into the conversation. The writing settles it.

‘Brutalist,’ [[Kim Petras]]. The most daring piece of writing of the year. Petras built it from a childhood memory: long drives across Germany with her architect father to get hormone treatment, him critiquing the concrete buildings they passed. The title does double duty, naming the architecture outside the car window and the hard, load-bearing resolve inside it. The chugging, Kraftwerk-style beat keeps the car moving, so the production serves the story instead of decorating it. It's a pop song about something pop rarely touches, told without a speech. On the chart, it spent three weeks at No. 1 and nine in the top 3.

‘Weather for Tennis,’ [[Hilary Duff]]. The surprise of the year on the page. Duff writes about a relationship where she keeps handing out second chances to someone who keeps breaking promises, then turns the camera on herself, tracing her own avoidance of conflict back to her parents' divorce. That self-implication is what lifts it above a breakup song. The title reads like a forecast for conditions that never quite arrive, which is exactly how the song feels. Written for an album she made with her husband, Matthew Koma, it's the most grown-up writing of her career. It debuted at No. 1 and stayed there for four weeks.

‘Bandaids,’ [[Katy Perry]]. A song carried by one image, and Perry commits to it: quick fixes on a wound too deep for them. The verses stack smaller pictures on top, flowers sent too late, splinters piling up, the slow sense of flatlining while trying to save something. The central metaphor is familiar, and some lines lean on it a little hard. But the closing turn, admitting she'd choose it all again, gives the song a grace her bigger hits rarely needed. Its 16 weeks make it the longest run in the field.

‘Stateside,’ [[Pink Pantheress]] and Zara Larsson. The best-built song in the field. Its subject is small, the first giddy rush of a crush, and it's stitched together from echoes of Adina Howard's ‘Freak Like Me’ and Groove Armada's ‘I See You Baby.’ Larsson's added verse turns it into a conversation across the Atlantic. As writing it's light, and voters may decide it belongs in Record of the Year. As construction it's close to flawless.

‘Cruel World,’ [[Holly Humberstone]]. A long-distance song about how the world itself seems to warp when the person you love isn't in it. Humberstone has always been strongest at small, specific feelings, and the title track of her second album points that skill at something sunnier without losing it. It peaked at No. 2 with five weeks in the top 3. That's close to the line of ‘Get Close,’ which won with a No. 2 peak.

‘Cranberry,’ [[girlsweetvoiced]]. The quietest writing in the race, and on purpose. It's a whispered, shy confession about everyday romance, the kind of song that works by holding back. Its gift is turning shyness itself into the hook.

Two dark horses with history. Kayla Rae's ‘True’ debuted at No. 2 on Dec. 4 and spent seven weeks in the top 3 without reaching No. 1, which is the same chart profile as her ‘Get Close,’ the winner at the 2021 show. [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘End of Your Love’ is the title track of an EP about letting go of the life you expected, written and produced with Alec Shaw, and it has spent the last three weeks at No. 1. Coleman has won this award before, with ‘Habit,’ and she's one of only three acts, with Gotye and Maroon 5, to take Song and Record of the Year on the same night.

The verdict. Plenty of songs had longer runs this year, and history says that won't decide anything. ‘Brutalist’ and ‘Weather for Tennis’ say the most and say it in ways only their writers could. ‘Bandaids’ is close behind on the strength of its ending, and ‘Cruel World’ has exactly the modest, well-placed run this category tends to reward. If Song of the Year is about the song, that's where it should be decided.

headline: Kenny Chesney is back in the top two for the first time since 2019
dek: “Silver Sands Marina” holds at No. 2, his best placing in almost seven years.
body: “Silver Sands Marina” holds at No. 2 on the Country Hot 20 this week, its second straight week in the runner-up spot. It is [[Kenny Chesney]]'s first top-two hit since “Tip of My Tongue” spent a week at No. 1 on November 14, 2019, almost seven years ago.
The song took the long road. It debuted at No. 18 on July 23 and spent four weeks at No. 7 before jumping five spots to No. 2 on October 8.
Chesney never went far in between. “Knowing You” in 2021 and “Just to Say We Did” in 2025 both stopped at No. 4. “Silver Sands Marina” is his 29th Hot 20 entry, his 24th top 10 and his 19th top 5.

linkText: Every #1 from the Pop 10's first months
headline: The Pop 10 turns 15
dek: How a high school drive became 15 years, 780 charts and 267 No. 1s.
body: The Pop 10 started the same fall I started driving. Once I had my own car in high school, the radio was on everywhere I went, and it pulled me into pop music in a way nothing had before. I grew to love the genre so much that I gave it a chart of its own. The first Pop 10 arrived on October 27, 2011, and David Guetta and Usher's ‘Without You’ was its first No. 1.

Before the Pop 10. Pop wasn't new to Willboard. During the transitional era, from January 2010 to October 2011, pop songs competed with country on the Hot 20. Shakira took ‘Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)’ all the way to No. 1 in 2010, and [[Demi Lovato]] did the same with ‘Skyscraper’ in 2011. [[Lady Gaga]] placed seven songs on the Hot 20, led by ‘Alejandro’ at No. 3.

The radio years (2011 to 2013). Dev's ‘In The Dark’ finished as the first Year-End No. 1. Then came the record that still stands: Gotye and Kimbra's ‘Somebody That I Used To Know’ spent 15 weeks at No. 1 in 2012 and 36 weeks on the chart. Bruno Mars followed with 11 weeks on top for ‘Locked Out of Heaven.’ In December 2013 the chart moved from feel to Spotify playlists.

The mid-2010s. [[Ariana Grande]] and Iggy Azalea's ‘Problem’ ruled 2014 with 10 weeks at No. 1. In 2015 [[Meghan Trainor]] arrived in a big way, taking the top two spots on the Year-End chart with ‘Like I'm Gonna Lose You’ and ‘Dear Future Husband.’ [[The Chainsmokers]] owned 2016 with nine weeks on top for ‘Don't Let Me Down,’ the start of a run that has made them the chart's second-longest leaders.

Counting the plays (2017 to now). Since December 2017 the Pop 10 has run on real play counts, first from Last.fm and since 2023 from stats.fm. Demi Lovato came full circle with ‘Sorry Not Sorry,’ the 2017 Year-End No. 1. Sam Smith topped the year twice, with ‘How Do You Sleep’ in 2019 and ‘Unholy’ with Kim Petras in 2022. In 2023 [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘Habit’ came within one week of Gotye's record with 14 weeks at No. 1. And the chart has gone global: Erika Vikman's ‘Ich Komme’ led for seven weeks in 2025, and the Pop Awards added Foreign Language Song of the Year to honor that year's music.

Milestones. The 100th song to reach No. 1 was Mariah Carey and YG's ‘I Don't’ on March 2, 2017. Meghan Trainor fittingly brought up No. 1 number 200 with ‘Made You Look’ on December 1, 2022, and Chloe Tang and Casandra's ‘Running on Blue’ became the 250th last December. Panic! At the Disco's ‘High Hopes’ was the 500th song ever to chart, in November 2018. The 1,000th was [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis,’ which debuted at No. 1 on March 5 of this year and was still on top a week later for the 750th Pop 10.

By the numbers. Through 780 charts, 267 different songs have reached No. 1. Meghan Trainor owns the record books with 13 No. 1s and 42 weeks on top, ahead of The Chainsmokers (34 weeks) and Ariana Grande (32). Here's to the next 15.

linkText: Dolly Parton's full Willboard chart history
headline: Dolly Parton's Willboard legacy: six hits, two charts, and records that still stand
dek: Two months after her death at 80, a look back at her years on the Hot 20 and the Pop 10.
body: [[Dolly Parton]] died on August 25 in Nashville at 80, and on Wednesday night the CMA's two-hour tribute brought country's biggest names together to sing her songs. Her catalog is far older than Willboard, but she found her way onto these charts six times over 13 years, and some of what she did here hasn't been matched.

Where it started. Her first appearance came in the chart's opening weeks. During the transitional era, ‘Jolene’ debuted at No. 14 on March 18, 2010, and climbed to No. 8 the next week, more than 35 years after its release. Its four-week run was the first sign that her songs don't belong to any one decade.

‘Home’ (2014). Her signature Willboard moment took patience. ‘Home’ debuted at No. 17 on July 10, 2014, and spent 14 weeks climbing before it reached No. 1 on October 9. It held the top spot for two weeks, spent 18 weeks on the chart and finished No. 14 on the 2014 Year-End chart. She was 68, and 12 years later she is still the oldest woman to top the Hot 20. The song also earned her a Music Video of the Year nomination at the 2015 Country Awards.

‘Pure and Simple’ (2016). The title track of her 2016 album entered at No. 20 on August 4 and made a slow, steady climb to No. 4, where it stayed for three weeks. Its 20-week run is her longest on any Willboard chart.

Crossing over (2019). Few country legends have topped the Pop 10, and Parton did it at 73. Galantis' ‘Faith,’ with Mr. Probz, debuted at No. 6 on November 28, 2019, and reached No. 1 two weeks later. It led for four straight weeks, carrying her into 2020, and finished No. 24 on the 2019 Pop Year-End chart. At the time she was the oldest act ever to top the Pop 10. Only Elton John and Cher have since topped it older, and Cher is the only woman to do it.

Still collaborating. She kept showing up alongside younger acts. ‘Happy All the Time’ with Sam Williams, Hank Williams' grandson, reached No. 12 on the Hot 20 in 2021, and ‘Bets On Us’ with Cheat Codes climbed to No. 5 on the Pop 10 in January 2023, her last Willboard hit.

By the numbers. Six chart entries, 65 weeks on the charts and six weeks at No. 1. She is one of only seven acts to send a song to No. 1 on both the Hot 20 and the Pop 10. Her legacy is much bigger than any chart, but on this one she left a mark that will be hard to touch.

headline: The Pop Awards honor the song, the record and the artist. Should they honor the voice?
dek: What a Best Vocal Performance award would reward, how the Grammys handled the same question, and the songs that would be in the running at the 2027 show.
body: The Pop Awards hand out six trophies: Artist, Record, Song, Album, New Artist and Foreign Language Song. Each one answers a different question. Song of the Year is about the writing. Record of the Year is about the finished production and how hard it landed on the Pop 10. Artist of the Year is about a whole year of work. None of them asks the simplest question a listener has: who actually sang the best? This piece makes the case for a Best Vocal Performance award, lays out how it could work and runs the 2027 field through it. This is a thought experiment, not an announcement, and nothing here changes the 2027 nominations.

What the award would honor. Best Vocal Performance would go to the singer, or singers, on one recording. Not the songwriters, not the producers and not the chart run. It rewards the take you hear: range and control, sure, but also phrasing, restraint, character and the moment where a voice turns a good song into a great one. A whispered vocal can win it as easily as a belted one. That makes it the one award where a modest chart hit can beat a long-running No. 1 on the merits, and it gives the show a category built for the singers who rarely win Record of the Year because their songs didn't run long enough.

How it mirrors the Grammys. The real-life Grammys have handed out vocal awards since the 1950s, and for decades they were split by gender: Best Female Pop Vocal Performance and Best Male Pop Vocal Performance. At the 54th Grammys in 2012, the Recording Academy folded both, along with Best Pop Instrumental Performance, into a single award, Best Pop Solo Performance. Adele won the first one for ‘Someone Like You,’ and Lola Young won it at the 2026 show for ‘Messy.’ A companion award, Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, covers records with more than one lead act. Both categories are for a single track, and the trophy goes to the performer, not the writers or producers. A Willboard version would follow the modern Grammy model: one award, no gender split, judged on a single recording. The country show already has Male and Female Vocalist of the Year, but those honor an artist's whole year. This would be the pop show's first award for one vocal on one record.

One award or two? The Grammys split solo acts from duos and groups. The Pop 10 history says the Pop Awards might need to as well. Seven of the 14 Record of the Year winners have been duos, groups or collaborations, from Gotye and Kimbra at the 2013 show to The Chainsmokers' ‘High’ at the 2023 show. Collaborations used to be even more common among nominees: 14 of 35 Record nominees from the 2013 to 2019 shows, but only about one in five since. The cleaner option is the Grammys' current setup in a smaller form: one Best Vocal Performance award, open to everyone, with every credited lead singer sharing a win. If duets keep turning up in the field, a separate Duo/Group award could follow later.

The rules. It would use the same window as every other Pop Award, roughly mid-November of one year to mid-November of the next, so the 2027 show covers songs from late 2025 through this fall. It would follow the show's existing rule that no song is nominated twice, which rules out the 2026 field, from ‘Bite My Tongue’ to ‘Honesty.’ The song would need to have charted on the Pop 10 in that window, with a peak cutoff like the top 3 to keep the field focused. One more rule matters: a vocal in any language counts. Foreign Language Song honors the song, but a voice doesn't need translating, and some of this year's strongest vocals weren't sung in English.

The front-runner: Cassandra Coleman, ‘End of Your Love.’ If one record this year was built around a voice, it's this one. It opens with just upright piano and her vocal, and the EP it comes from was recorded with a full band in one room, so what you hear is close to a live take. It reached No. 1 and held for three weeks. Coleman already swept Record and Song of the Year at the 2024 show with ‘Habit.’ She's also the field's deepest bench, with ‘Maggie’ at No. 1 and ‘Dying Star’ and ‘Midnight Blue’ in the top 3, though only one of her songs should make the cut.

The duets. Two duet records would make a strong case. ‘Liekinheitin’ by Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen won Finland's UMK this year, and critics singled out Parkkonen's vocal and the chemistry between his voice and Lampenius's violin, which answer each other through the song before its big climax. It spent a week at No. 1 and six in the top 3. Then there's ‘Bring Your Love,’ the Madonna and Sabrina Carpenter duet that debuted at Coachella and won Best Collaboration at the VMAs. It peaked at No. 2. Two eras of pop voices on one record is exactly what a vocal award is for.

The safe bets. Holly Humberstone's ‘Cruel World’ is a diaristic song about a long-distance relationship, and she has called it her favorite song she has written. It peaked at No. 2 with five weeks in the top 3, and quiet, confessional vocals like this are the kind the Grammy category has rewarded. Demi Lovato has two contenders, ‘In My Head’ (No. 1) and ‘Sorry to Myself’ (No. 2), and her voice has carried a Record of the Year winner before, ‘Sorry Not Sorry’ at the 2018 show. Kayla Rae's ‘True’ (No. 2, seven weeks in the top 3) fits here too.

The dark horses. girlsweetvoiced's ‘Cranberry’ is the opposite of a showcase: a whispered vocal that still ran three weeks at No. 1. A vocal award that only rewards power would miss it, and a good one wouldn't. Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me,’ the nu-metal entry that finished third at Eurovision in Vienna, is the loudest vocal in the field and spent four weeks at No. 1. Kehlani's ‘Folded’ peaked at No. 3. Karol G's ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ is a No. 1 sung in Spanish, and it makes the case for the language rule.

Where the panel lands. Mitzi Tallyho, Willboard's chart data editor, notes that a vocal award would break the pattern of Record of the Year, which the year's biggest hit has won 12 times in 14 shows. ‘Obsexxed’ and ‘Brutalist’ top the 2026 chart race, but neither is a natural pick here. Sebastian Crescendo, Willboard's senior critic, goes with Cassandra Coleman: ‘You build a vocal award for a record like “End of Your Love.” Everything else gets out of the way of the voice.’ Bobbie Jo Rhinestone of the Windows Down podcast takes ‘Liekinheitin’: ‘Nobody I know understands a word of it, and everybody I know has sung along to it in the car.’

The verdict. The Pop Awards already reward the biggest hits, and they should. A Best Vocal Performance award would reward something the chart can't measure. It would follow the Grammys' modern single-award model, stay open to any language and give a trophy to the records people remember for the voice. If it existed at the 2027 show, the smart pick would be ‘End of Your Love,’ the duet to watch would be ‘Liekinheitin,’ and the upset everyone would argue about would be ‘Cranberry.’
